messages_body:
Hi Priya,

We're responding from HealthSync where we just completed a forensic review of a recent user-impacting bug. Our internal investigators want to retain full tenant debug and request logs for the affected tenant for 180 days so the SRE and our retained forensics partner can finish root cause analysis.

Per our SOC 2 auditor and upcoming SIG/CAIQ review, they will ask Redwood to produce: a copy of the preserved logs, an export manifest showing hashes, and an attestation that data was not modified and was deleted at the end of the hold. Is Redwood able to grant a tenant-specific retention exception and provide the artifacts? If so, what evidence package and timelines should we expect?

We'd like to formalize this today if possible — happy to sign any exception form.

Alex
Alex Rivera
Incident Response Lead, HealthSync

--
Attachment: incident_summary.txt (plain text, 6KB)

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and context. We can support a temporary tenant-level hold, but we'll need to follow our exception workflow so we capture approvals and produce the necessary evidence for SOC 2/SIG reviewers.

Quick outline: 1) We require a signed Retention Exception Form (I've attached a template). 2) Security will create a read-only export of the requested log buckets and generate a manifest with SHA256 checksums. 3) Legal must sign off on the hold length and data categories retained. 4) We will produce an evidence matrix (example attached) aligning items to SOC 2 control IDs and CAIQ questions.

I'm looping in Jonas (Legal) and Neha (Security) to scope any legal or technical constraints — marissa from CS will help coordinate the export delivery and timing.

Proposed target timeline: signed form within 48 hours, export & manifest within 3 business days after signatures, evidentiary package (matrix + sample export) within 5 business days. If HealthSync needs 180 days retention, we will document the exception and include the TTL in the form.

Can you confirm the exact tenant ID(s), the retention window you need (you said 180 days), and whether the logs include customer PII? If there is PII we will need a limited-scope redaction plan and legal approval.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

On Tue, May 1, 2028 at 9:12 AM Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@healthsync.com> wrote:
> We're responding from HealthSync where we just completed a forensic review..."

Thanks Priya — adding legal notes.

High-level constraints from Legal: we can approve tenant-specific retention exceptions provided: (a) the scope is limited and documented, (b) retention timeframe is explicit in an approved form, (c) we capture an owner and deletion trigger, and (d) we log any access to preserved data during the exception.

Two items to highlight: 1) If preserved logs contain PII, we should require HealthSync to take on the responsibility to redact before any external sharing, or sign a data processing addendum amendment that clarifies responsibilities. 2) For the SOC 2 evidence packet, we should map each requested artifact to common control IDs (CC6.1, CC7.2, etc.) so auditors can validate completeness; the evidence matrix Priya mentioned is exactly the right approach.

I've drafted a short checklist that Security should complete before we hand over any export: manifest + hashes, access audit for the preserved object, retention metadata with TTL set, and confirmation that deletion automation is scheduled at the exception end date.

Looping in Neha for the technical steps.

- Jonas (Legal)

On Tue, May 1, 2028 at 10:08 AM Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.example> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the clear ask and context..."

Priya / Alex — technical plan from Security below.

We can create a tenant-scoped snapshot of the requested log indexes and put them in a read-only storage bucket with lifecycle metadata. Steps:
1) Create export job that captures the requested date ranges and indices; encrypt with customer-specific KEK and generate per-file SHA256 checksums.
2) Store export in a locked bucket with object-level immutability for the exception window. No internal writes will be allowed except by a small, auditable group.
3) Produce an export manifest (file list + hashes), an access log showing any GETs on the preserved artifacts, and a signed attestation from Security that the files were not modified.
4) At exception expiry (180 days), the deletion automation will run and we will provide a Proof of Destroy report (manifest of removed object names + deletion timestamps).

We will need HealthSync to confirm whether the export contains PII. If it does, we will require either a redaction process prior to transfer to them or a documented acceptance that they will handle redaction.

Attachments: redwood_evidence_matrix.xlsx (mapping template).

- Neha (Security)

On Tue, May 1, 2028 at 11:45 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.example> wrote:

Alex — good news: we have legal and security alignment on the mechanics. Next steps from our side to finalize: 1) HealthSync fills and signs the Retention Exception Form and returns it to legalops@healthsync.com (cc marissa.cole@redwood.example). 2) We will issue a DocuSign packet with the exception statement and data handling addendum for PII (if applicable). 3) Security will schedule the export job after DocuSign completes. 4) Redwood will produce a consolidated evidence packet (evidence matrix + sample export + attestation + access logs + PoD) at the end of the export window and again after deletion.

Action items for HealthSync: provide tenant ID(s), indicate whether export includes PII, and sign the attached exception form.

I will prepare the DocuSign and a short legal addendum this afternoon. Priya — please coordinate the CS delivery window with HealthSync and confirm who should receive the sample export (SFTP vs. secure Drive).

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention_exception_form.pdf, redwood_evidence_matrix.xlsx
